The United States government has suspended several large technology companies, including Microsoft and Adobe, from a programme for skilled foreign workers. Vice President JD Vance announced the decision at a news conference on Thursday, 8 October. He said the government is also investigating the companies for possible fraud.

The programme gives skilled workers from other countries a way to live in the US permanently. A permanent residence permit is often called a "green card". Many technology companies also use H-1B visas, which let them employ foreign specialists for a limited time. President Donald Trump's government wants companies to employ more Americans instead.

Vance said Microsoft dismissed 6,000 American workers while it received 6,300 H-1B visas and almost 3,000 green cards. The Labor Department says it has found visa fraud worth 22 billion dollars. Microsoft's share price fell 7.5 percent after the news. Neither company has commented, and it is not yet clear how long the suspension will last.

sents.en: The United States government has suspended several large technology companies, including Microsoft and Adobe, from a programme for skilled foreign workers.
sents.tr: Amerika Birleşik Devletleri hükümeti, aralarında Microsoft ve Adobe'un da bulunduğu birkaç büyük teknoloji şirketini nitelikli yabancı çalışanlara yönelik bir programdan geçici olarak çıkardı.

sents.en: Vice President JD Vance announced the decision at a news conference on Thursday, 8 October.
sents.tr: Başkan Yardımcısı JD Vance kararı 8 Ekim Perşembe günü düzenlediği basın toplantısında açıkladı.

sents.en: He said the government is also investigating the companies for possible fraud.
sents.tr: Vance, hükümetin bu şirketleri olası dolandırıcılık nedeniyle de soruşturduğunu söyledi.

sents.en: The programme gives skilled workers from other countries a way to live in the US permanently.
sents.tr: Bu program, başka ülkelerden gelen nitelikli çalışanlara ABD'de kalıcı olarak yaşama yolu açıyor.

sents.en: A permanent residence permit is often called a "green card".
sents.tr: Kalıcı oturma iznine genellikle "yeşil kart" (green card) deniyor.

sents.en: Many technology companies also use H-1B visas, which let them employ foreign specialists for a limited time.
sents.tr: Birçok teknoloji şirketi ayrıca, yabancı uzmanları sınırlı bir süre için çalıştırmalarına izin veren H-1B vizelerini kullanıyor.

sents.en: President Donald Trump's government wants companies to employ more Americans instead.
sents.tr: Başkan Donald Trump'ın hükümeti ise şirketlerin bunun yerine daha fazla Amerikalı çalıştırmasını istiyor.

sents.en: Vance said Microsoft dismissed 6,000 American workers while it received 6,300 H-1B visas and almost 3,000 green cards.
sents.tr: Vance, Microsoft'un 6.000 Amerikalı çalışanı işten çıkarırken 6.300 H-1B vizesi ve yaklaşık 3.000 yeşil kart aldığını söyledi.

sents.en: The Labor Department says it has found visa fraud worth 22 billion dollars.
sents.tr: Çalışma Bakanlığı, 22 milyar dolarlık vize dolandırıcılığı tespit ettiğini söylüyor.

sents.en: Microsoft's share price fell 7.5 percent after the news.
sents.tr: Haberin ardından Microsoft'un hisse fiyatı yüzde 7,5 düştü.

sents.en: Neither company has commented, and it is not yet clear how long the suspension will last.
sents.tr: İki şirket de açıklama yapmadı; uygulamanın ne kadar süreceği de henüz belli değil.

Archaeologists in central Türkiye have found a large collection of clay tablets from the Hittite kingdom. Culture and Tourism Minister Mehmet Nuri Ersoy announced the discovery on Thursday, 8 October. This year's excavations at Kayalıpınar, in Sivas province, produced 131 tablets and pieces of tablets.

The Hittites ruled much of Anatolia more than 3,000 years ago. They wrote in cuneiform, a system of small wedge-shaped marks pressed into wet clay. The new texts are about 3,400 years old and come from the time of King Tudhaliya II.

Together with last year's finds, the archive now has 184 pieces. Ersoy called it the largest Hittite-language archive discovered in this century. The tablets describe a disease with high fever that spread between cities and mainly affected children. They also record the death and funeral of a baby princess. In another text, generals ask the king for more soldiers, horses and chariots. The texts should help researchers understand Hittite history and religion better.

sents.en: Archaeologists in central Türkiye have found a large collection of clay tablets from the Hittite kingdom.
sents.tr: Türkiye'nin orta kesiminde arkeologlar, Hitit krallığından kalma büyük bir kil tablet koleksiyonu buldu.

sents.en: Culture and Tourism Minister Mehmet Nuri Ersoy announced the discovery on Thursday, 8 October.
sents.tr: Kültür ve Turizm Bakanı Mehmet Nuri Ersoy keşfi 8 Ekim Perşembe günü duyurdu.

sents.en: This year's excavations at Kayalıpınar, in Sivas province, produced 131 tablets and pieces of tablets.
sents.tr: Sivas'taki Kayalıpınar'da bu yıl yapılan kazılarda 131 tablet ve tablet parçası çıkarıldı.

sents.en: The Hittites ruled much of Anatolia more than 3,000 years ago.
sents.tr: Hititler 3.000 yıldan uzun süre önce Anadolu'nun büyük bölümüne hükmediyordu.

sents.en: They wrote in cuneiform, a system of small wedge-shaped marks pressed into wet clay.
sents.tr: Yaş kile bastırılan küçük, kama biçimli işaretlerden oluşan bir sistem olan çivi yazısını kullanıyorlardı.

sents.en: The new texts are about 3,400 years old and come from the time of King Tudhaliya II.
sents.tr: Yeni metinler yaklaşık 3.400 yıllık ve Kral II. Tudhaliya dönemine ait.

sents.en: Together with last year's finds, the archive now has 184 pieces.
sents.tr: Geçen yılın buluntularıyla birlikte arşivde artık 184 parça var.

sents.en: Ersoy called it the largest Hittite-language archive discovered in this century.
sents.tr: Ersoy bunu, bu yüzyılda keşfedilen en kapsamlı Hititçe arşiv olarak nitelendirdi.

sents.en: The tablets describe a disease with high fever that spread between cities and mainly affected children.
sents.tr: Tabletler, şehirler arasında yayılan ve en çok çocukları etkileyen yüksek ateşli bir hastalığı anlatıyor.

sents.en: They also record the death and funeral of a baby princess.
sents.tr: Ayrıca bebek yaştaki bir prensesin ölümünü ve cenaze törenini de kaydediyor.

sents.en: In another text, generals ask the king for more soldiers, horses and chariots.
sents.tr: Başka bir metinde komutanlar kraldan daha fazla asker, at ve savaş arabası istiyor.

sents.en: The texts should help researchers understand Hittite history and religion better.
sents.tr: Metinlerin, araştırmacıların Hitit tarihini ve dinini daha iyi anlamasına yardımcı olması bekleniyor.

items.title: 3,400-year-old Hittite royal archive found in Sivas
items.tr: Sivas'taki Kayalıpınar kazılarında bu yıl 131 Hitit tableti ve parçası bulundu; arşiv toplam 184 parçaya ulaştı. Tabletler bir salgını, bir prensesin ölümünü ve komutanların kraldan asker istemesini anlatıyor.

Sailors who take oil tankers through the Strait of Hormuz are now earning much more than usual, Al Jazeera reported on Thursday, 8 October. According to the Financial Times, some captains receive a bonus of 50,000 dollars for a single voyage. Whole crews can earn four to six times their normal pay.

The Strait of Hormuz is a narrow sea passage between Iran and Oman. Ships must pass through it to carry oil from the Gulf countries to the rest of the world. Since the war between the US, Israel and Iran began in late February, Iran has mostly closed the passage and attacks ships that cross without permission.

The work is dangerous. Shipping managers believe the chance of being hit during a crossing is about one in twenty. Crews turn off their lights and put sandbags on deck as protection against drones and missiles. Analysts expect more attacks, so oil prices will probably stay high.

sents.tr: Financial Times'a göre bazı kaptanlar tek bir sefer için 50.000 dolar ikramiye alıyor.

sents.en: Whole crews can earn four to six times their normal pay.

People who want to buy a home in the Netherlands had a little more choice this summer. The estate agents' association NVM published its figures for July, August and September on Thursday, 8 October. About 39,000 existing homes were for sale at the end of September, 24 percent more than a year earlier.

The Dutch housing market has been very tight for years: there are too few homes, so buyers often offer more than the asking price. The asking price is the amount the seller requests. One reason for the extra supply is that landlords are selling apartments they used to rent out.

The average home sold for 503,000 euros, 1.8 percent more than last year. Almost two-thirds of homes still sold above the asking price, compared with 71 percent a year ago. In Amsterdam the price reached a record 7,401 euros per square metre. NVM says buyers now have more time to look and sometimes room to negotiate.

sents.en: People who want to buy a home in the Netherlands had a little more choice this summer.
sents.tr: Hollanda'da ev almak isteyenlerin bu yaz biraz daha fazla seçeneği oldu.

sents.en: The estate agents' association NVM published its figures for July, August and September on Thursday, 8 October.
sents.tr: Emlakçılar birliği NVM, temmuz, ağustos ve eylül aylarına ait verilerini 8 Ekim Perşembe günü yayımladı.

sents.en: About 39,000 existing homes were for sale at the end of September, 24 percent more than a year earlier.
sents.tr: Eylül sonunda yaklaşık 39.000 mevcut konut satılıktı; bu, bir yıl öncesine göre yüzde 24 daha fazla.

sents.en: The Dutch housing market has been very tight for years: there are too few homes, so buyers often offer more than the asking price.
sents.tr: Hollanda konut piyasası yıllardır çok sıkışık: yeterince ev yok, bu yüzden alıcılar çoğu zaman istenen fiyattan fazlasını teklif ediyor.

sents.en: The asking price is the amount the seller requests.
sents.tr: İstenen fiyat, satıcının talep ettiği tutardır.

sents.en: One reason for the extra supply is that landlords are selling apartments they used to rent out.
sents.tr: Arzın artmasının bir nedeni, ev sahiplerinin eskiden kiraya verdikleri daireleri satması.

sents.en: The average home sold for 503,000 euros, 1.8 percent more than last year.
sents.tr: Ortalama bir ev 503.000 avroya satıldı; bu, geçen yıla göre yüzde 1,8 daha fazla.

sents.en: Almost two-thirds of homes still sold above the asking price, compared with 71 percent a year ago.
sents.tr: Evlerin neredeyse üçte ikisi hâlâ istenen fiyatın üzerinde satıldı; bir yıl önce bu oran yüzde 71'di.

sents.en: In Amsterdam the price reached a record 7,401 euros per square metre.
sents.tr: Amsterdam'da fiyat metrekare başına 7.401 avro ile rekor kırdı.

sents.en: NVM says buyers now have more time to look and sometimes room to negotiate.
sents.tr: NVM, alıcıların artık evlere bakmak için daha fazla zamanı ve bazen pazarlık payı olduğunu söylüyor.

items.title: Dutch home buyers get more choice as supply grows

Istanbul has 1,238 buildings that could fall down by themselves, according to figures from the city government. The number received new attention on Thursday, 8 October, after part of a seven-storey apartment building collapsed in the Maltepe district.

Istanbul lies close to a major earthquake fault, and many of its buildings are old. After the big earthquakes of February 2023 in southern Türkiye, thousands of people a day asked the city for a quick safety test. Inspectors check the quality of the concrete and steel and compare the building with its original plan.

Most of the dangerous buildings are in the districts of Avcılar, Zeytinburnu, Bağcılar and Bahçelievler. So far the city has received about 170,000 requests and has examined around 40,000 buildings. Interest has fallen: only about 500 people a day now ask for a test. A city official, Murat Yun, told the television channel NTV that about 100,000 people have already moved to safe homes.

sents.en: Istanbul has 1,238 buildings that could fall down by themselves, according to figures from the city government.
sents.tr: Büyükşehir belediyesinin verilerine göre İstanbul'da kendiliğinden çökebilecek 1.238 bina var.

sents.en: The number received new attention on Thursday, 8 October, after part of a seven-storey apartment building collapsed in the Maltepe district.
sents.tr: Bu sayı, Maltepe ilçesinde yedi katlı bir apartmanın bir bölümünün çökmesinin ardından 8 Ekim Perşembe günü yeniden gündeme geldi.

sents.en: Istanbul lies close to a major earthquake fault, and many of its buildings are old.
sents.tr: İstanbul büyük bir deprem fay hattının yakınında yer alıyor ve binalarının çoğu eski.

sents.en: After the big earthquakes of February 2023 in southern Türkiye, thousands of people a day asked the city for a quick safety test.
sents.tr: Türkiye'nin güneyinde Şubat 2023'te yaşanan büyük depremlerin ardından günde binlerce kişi belediyeden hızlı güvenlik testi istedi.

sents.en: Inspectors check the quality of the concrete and steel and compare the building with its original plan.
sents.tr: Denetçiler betonun ve demirin kalitesini kontrol ediyor ve binayı ilk projesiyle karşılaştırıyor.

sents.en: A city official, Murat Yun, told the television channel NTV that about 100,000 people have already moved to safe homes.

Another person in the Netherlands has died after catching West Nile virus. The public health institute RIVM reported this on Thursday, 8 October, in its weekly update. Ten of the 59 people who got the virus in the country this year have now died.

West Nile virus lives mainly in birds. Mosquitoes that bite an infected bird can then give the virus to people or horses. Most infected people do not feel ill at all, but the virus can be dangerous for some. RIVM says the people who died were old or already had health problems, and the virus was not always the direct cause of death.

Only three new infections were found in the first week of October. The number is falling, as RIVM expected, because the mosquito season is ending and the weather is getting colder. The virus was also found in 13 more horses, so 163 horses have been infected this year.
items.title: Tenth person dies after West Nile virus infection in Netherlands
items.tr: Hollanda'da Batı Nil virüsüne yakalanan bir kişi daha öldü; bu yıl virüs bulaşan 59 kişiden 10'u hayatını kaybetti. Sivrisinek mevsimi bittiği için yeni vaka sayısı azalıyor.

Dutch Defence Minister Dilan Yeşilgöz called Russia "the enemy" on Thursday. She said it in parliament in The Hague, during a debate about the defence budget. Before, she used a softer word and called Russia "the aggressor".

An aggressor is a country that attacks another one, as Russia did when it invaded Ukraine in 2022. The word "enemy" is stronger: it describes a country that is a direct danger to you. Yeşilgöz pointed to more sabotage, drone incidents and threats in Europe. Dutch intelligence services also warn that Russia is preparing for a possible conflict with NATO, the Western military alliance.

The minister said the Netherlands is not at war and that its policy does not change immediately. The country will keep spending more on defence and working closely with its allies. Russia's embassy in The Hague reacted angrily. It asked whether she spoke for the whole government and accused the Netherlands of looking for a conflict.

sents.en: Dutch Defence Minister Dilan Yeşilgöz called Russia "the enemy" on Thursday.
sents.tr: Hollanda Savunma Bakanı Dilan Yeşilgöz perşembe günü Rusya'yı "düşman" olarak nitelendirdi.

sents.tr: Bunu Lahey'deki parlamentoda, savunma bütçesi görüşmeleri sırasında söyledi.

sents.en: Before, she used a softer word and called Russia "the aggressor".
sents.tr: Daha önce daha yumuşak bir sözcük kullanıyor ve Rusya'ya "saldırgan" diyordu.

sents.en: An aggressor is a country that attacks another one, as Russia did when it invaded Ukraine in 2022.
sents.tr: Saldırgan, Rusya'nın 2022'de Ukrayna'yı işgal ederken yaptığı gibi, başka bir ülkeye saldıran ülkedir.

sents.en: The word "enemy" is stronger: it describes a country that is a direct danger to you.
sents.tr: "Düşman" sözcüğü daha güçlüdür: sizin için doğrudan tehlike oluşturan bir ülkeyi anlatır.

sents.tr: Bakanın tüm hükümet adına konuşup konuşmadığını sordu ve Hollanda'yı çatışma aramakla suçladı.

Italy's parliament approved a new election law on Thursday. The lower house, the Chamber of Deputies, voted 227 to 164 in favour in a secret vote. Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni's right-wing government wrote the law for the next national election in 2027.

Meloni has led Italy since 2022. Under the new rules, parties get seats in parliament according to their share of the votes. There is also a bonus: a group of parties that wins more than 42% of the votes receives extra seats, so that it has a clear majority. The government says this will bring political stability.

The opposition voted against the law. It says the law was designed to help Meloni win again, and it plans to ask a court to cancel it. Some experts think the law could also help the centre-left, if its divided parties join together. The bonus is 70 extra seats in the lower house and 35 in the Senate, the upper house.

sents.en: Italy's parliament approved a new election law on Thursday.
sents.tr: İtalya parlamentosu perşembe günü yeni bir seçim yasasını onayladı.

sents.en: The lower house, the Chamber of Deputies, voted 227 to 164 in favour in a secret vote.
sents.tr: Alt kanat olan Temsilciler Meclisi, gizli oylamada 164'e karşı 227 oyla yasayı kabul etti.

sents.en: Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni's right-wing government wrote the law for the next national election in 2027.
sents.tr: Yasayı Başbakan Giorgia Meloni'nin sağcı hükümeti, 2027'deki bir sonraki genel seçim için hazırladı.

sents.en: Meloni has led Italy since 2022.
sents.tr: Meloni 2022'den beri İtalya'yı yönetiyor.

sents.en: Under the new rules, parties get seats in parliament according to their share of the votes.
sents.tr: Yeni kurallara göre partiler, aldıkları oy oranına göre parlamentoda sandalye kazanıyor.

sents.en: There is also a bonus: a group of parties that wins more than 42% of the votes receives extra seats, so that it has a clear majority.
sents.tr: Bir de ikramiye var: oyların %42'sinden fazlasını alan parti grubu, net bir çoğunluğa sahip olması için ek sandalye alıyor.

sents.en: The government says this will bring political stability.
sents.tr: Hükümet bunun siyasi istikrar getireceğini söylüyor.

sents.en: The opposition voted against the law.
sents.tr: Muhalefet yasaya karşı oy kullandı.

sents.en: It says the law was designed to help Meloni win again, and it plans to ask a court to cancel it.
sents.tr: Muhalefet, yasanın Meloni'nin yeniden kazanmasına yardım etmek için tasarlandığını söylüyor ve iptali için mahkemeye başvurmayı planlıyor.

sents.en: Some experts think the law could also help the centre-left, if its divided parties join together.
sents.tr: Bazı uzmanlar, bölünmüş partileri bir araya gelirse yasanın merkez sola da yarayabileceğini düşünüyor.

sents.en: The bonus is 70 extra seats in the lower house and 35 in the Senate, the upper house.

The United States would never allow a war between Greece and Türkiye, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has said. He called such a conflict "unthinkable" in an interview with the Greek newspaper Kathimerini, published on Thursday after his visit to Athens.

The Secretary of State is the American foreign minister. Greece and Türkiye are both members of NATO, the Western military alliance, but they have argued for decades about sea borders in the Aegean and about the divided island of Cyprus. The newest argument is about an electricity cable planned under the sea between Greece and Cyprus.

Rubio also spoke about F-35 fighter jets. Türkiye was removed from the F-35 programme in 2019 because it bought the S-400 air defence system from Russia. Rubio said President Donald Trump wants Türkiye to get the jets if possible, since it has already paid for some. But American law sets strict conditions, and the problem is not solved yet.

Türkiye's government will present new measures to make schools safer in February 2027. Education Minister Yusuf Tekin said this on Thursday in an interview with the TV channel Haber Global. He did not explain what the new measures will be.

Türkiye has seen several attacks by students at schools since April. In that month, a student attacked his school in the southern province of Kahramanmaraş, and nine students and a teacher died. After that, the government put metal detectors at school doors and hired 25,000 security workers across the country.

This week, one student died in a knife attack at a middle school in Istanbul. Tekin called the attacks an "epidemic", a word normally used for a disease that spreads quickly. He said police measures alone are not enough and that parents have a very important role. Parents of children who started primary or middle school this year had to complete a course called "Parent School".
items.title: Türkiye plans new school safety measures for February
items.tr: Millî Eğitim Bakanı Yusuf Tekin, okullardaki saldırılara karşı yeni bir güvenlik paketinin Şubat 2027'de açıklanacağını söyledi. Tekin, yalnızca polis önlemlerinin yeterli olmadığını ve velilerin rolünün çok önemli olduğunu vurguladı.

Sales of fully electric cars in the European Union rose by 45% in the first eight months of 2026. People bought 1.64 million of them, says a new report by Transport & Environment, a European organisation that works for cleaner transport.

A fully electric car has no petrol or diesel engine and runs only on a battery. Now car makers are bringing cheaper models to the market. About 60 new electric models are expected in Europe this year. By the end of the year, buyers should have 16 models that cost less than €25,000.

In August, 28% of new cars sold in the EU were electric. Between April and June, electric cars sold better than petrol-only cars for the first time. The report says that an electric car charged at home costs about half as much to run as a petrol or diesel car. It warns that growth will slow if the EU weakens its pollution rules for cars.
items.title: Electric car sales in the EU rise 45%
items.tr: AB'de tamamen elektrikli otomobil satışları 2026'nın ilk sekiz ayında %45 artarak 1,64 milyona ulaştı. Rapora göre daha ucuz modeller pazarı büyütüyor.

Many people in the Netherlands are thinking about spending New Year's Eve in Germany this year. The reason is a new ban: for the first time, ordinary people in the whole country may not set off fireworks. The regional broadcaster RTV Oost reported the trend this week.

Setting off fireworks at midnight on 31 December is an old Dutch tradition. But every year it causes many injuries, fires and damage, so parliament decided to ban it. In Germany, people can still buy and use fireworks around New Year.

The travel website Booking.com says searches for places to stay in Gronau, a German town just across the border from Enschede, rose by 214%. These numbers show searches, not real bookings. Hotels in Gronau say they do not see many more Dutch guests yet. Bringing fireworks back from Germany is not allowed. The fine is at least €100, and the police plan to set up checkpoints.
items.title: Dutch look to Germany as fireworks ban begins
items.tr: Hollanda'da bu yılbaşında ilk kez ülke genelinde havai fişek yasağı uygulanacak. Booking.com'a göre birçok Hollandalı yılbaşı için sınırın hemen ötesindeki Alman kasabalarında konaklama arıyor.

The Canadian writer Anne Carson has won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature. The Swedish Academy announced its decision in Stockholm on Thursday, 8 October. Carson is 76 years old and works as a poet, essayist and translator.

The Nobel Prize in Literature is the world's most famous prize for writers. The Swedish Academy chooses the winner every year. Carson is also a scholar of ancient Greek, and her books mix poetry with prose and bring Greek myths into modern life. Her best-known book, "Autobiography of Red" from 1998, is a novel written as a poem. It turns an old Greek poem about the hero Heracles into the story of a modern boy.

The Academy praised her bold and inventive work, which creates new forms of literature. Carson is only the 19th woman to receive this prize. She will get 12 million Swedish kronor, about 1.07 million euros. The ceremony takes place in Stockholm on 10 December.

Türkiye will help Saudi Arabia to defend itself, but it will not send soldiers to attack another country. Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said this in Ankara on Thursday, 8 October. He spoke at a press conference with Hungary's foreign minister, Anita Orbán.

The background is the Mecca Alliance, a defence agreement that Türkiye, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan signed in August 2026. Under it, an attack on one member counts as an attack on all three. The Houthis, an armed group in Yemen, have recently attacked Saudi oil and military sites. On Monday, the three countries promised military help to Saudi Arabia.

Fidan called the agreement a pact for defence, not for attack. The agreement was given to President Erdoğan on Wednesday and will soon go to parliament for approval. The opposition says no troops may go to Saudi Arabia before that vote, but Fidan rejected this. According to the newspaper Sabah, Türkiye may provide air defence systems and drone technology.

Online bullying is growing again in the Netherlands, and artificial intelligence (AI) plays a bigger part in it. The organisation Offlimits reported this on Thursday, 8 October. It sees more and more fake pictures that schoolchildren make to humiliate classmates or teachers.

Offlimits is a Dutch expertise centre for online abuse. With modern AI tools, anyone can quickly make a realistic picture of something that never happened. Young people told Offlimits about fake images in which they kiss, dance or vomit.

From January to September 2026, Offlimits received 955 reports of online bullying or abuse. In all of 2025 there were 860, and in 2024 only 298. AI images now make up 17.4 percent of the reports, compared with 2 percent in 2024. Babette Keuning of Offlimits says bullying no longer stays at school but continues on the phone at home. Offlimits advises parents and schools to talk with children about online behaviour early and often.

The Greek airline Aegean is at the top of a new safety ranking of European airlines. The company AirAdvisor published the ranking, and Aegean received 89 points out of 100. Ryanair came second with 86 points, and Austrian Airlines third with 85.5.

The index compares 20 large airlines: ten low-cost airlines and ten traditional ones. A low-cost airline sells cheap tickets and asks extra money for bags and meals. The biggest part of the score, 40 percent, depends on accidents between 2016 and 2025. The rest looks at safety checks, the age of the planes, pilot training and finances.

Three of the top five are low-cost airlines: Ryanair, Norwegian and SunExpress, which belongs to Turkish Airlines and Lufthansa. Turkish Airlines and Lufthansa share ninth place with 83 points, and Pegasus is last with 64.5. AirAdvisor says the numbers do not show that cheap tickets mean more risk. The index only compares airlines; it does not call any airline unsafe.
items.title: Greek airline Aegean tops European safety ranking

The Dutch airline KLM will give passengers free, fast internet on its long flights to other continents. The company announced this on Thursday, 8 October. The service will start in the middle of 2027, said KLM's chief executive, Marjan Rintel.

KLM will use Starlink, a service of the American company SpaceX, which Elon Musk leads. Older internet systems on planes use stations on the ground or satellites that are very far from the Earth. Starlink uses a large number of satellites that fly much lower. Because the signal travels a shorter distance, the connection is faster.

Passengers will be able to visit websites, send emails and messages, and watch films and series during the flight. The free internet is for members of Flying Blue, the customer programme of KLM and Air France. Other passengers can join before the flight or on board. KLM has already started to bring free internet to its planes on European routes.
items.title: KLM will offer free fast internet on long flights
items.tr: KLM, 2027 ortasından itibaren kıtalararası uçuşlarında Starlink uyduları üzerinden ücretsiz ve hızlı internet sunacak. Hizmetten Flying Blue üyeleri yararlanabilecek.

A coffee museum has opened in an Ottoman mansion that is almost 200 years old. The building stands in Safranbolu, a historic town in northern Türkiye. For many years it was a hotel and restaurant, but it closed more than a year ago.

Safranbolu is famous for its old Ottoman houses and has been on UNESCO's World Heritage List since 1994. The Havuzlu Asmazlar Mansion was built in 1830 for Hüseyin Çavuş Bey, who governed the town. The Turkish Touring and Automobile Association bought it in 1976, repaired it and opened it as a small hotel in 1988.

The most special part of the mansion is a pool inside the house. The museum's founder, Semih Yıldırım, says the water protected the house against fire. Its sound also kept the governor's meetings private, because people nearby could not understand the words. In the museum, visitors can rest in the garden and learn about the history of coffee.
items.title: Old Ottoman mansion in Safranbolu becomes coffee museum
items.tr: Safranbolu'da 1830'da yapılan Havuzlu Asmazlar Konağı'nın bir bölümü kahve müzesi olarak açıldı. Yıllarca otel olarak kullanılan konak, evin içindeki havuzuyla tanınıyor.

Scientists have identified a new kind of ancient crocodile from Egypt. The animal lived about 45 million years ago, in a warm, shallow sea that covered what is now northern Egypt. The study appeared in the journal Royal Society Open Science.

The almost complete skull was dug up in the 1920s, and experts placed it in a known group of crocodiles. It comes from the Mokattam Formation, a layer of limestone near Cairo. The Great Sphinx and the pyramids of Giza are made of stone from the same layer.

Now researchers have studied the skull again with CT scans, which show the inside of an object. They compared more than 300 features with other crocodiles, living and extinct, and found enough differences for a new name: Herugavialis cairensis. "Heru" is another name for the Egyptian god Horus. The skull has lost the tip of its nose, just like the Sphinx. Today only two related species survive, both in Asia.

A seven-floor apartment building partly collapsed in Istanbul early on Thursday, 8 October. Its three lowest floors fell down. By late morning, rescue teams had found two bodies and were still searching for two more people. Ten people were saved, and three of them are children.

The building stands in Maltepe, a district on the Asian side of the city. Nobody knows yet why it collapsed. Weak buildings are a serious worry in Istanbul, a city of about 16 million people with a high earthquake risk. City data show that 1,238 buildings could fall down even without an earthquake.

Emergency services received the call at about 5:40 in the morning. Search dogs helped rescuers to find four people alive under the rubble, the broken pieces of the building. The governor, Davut Gül, said none of the rescued people is in danger of dying. Officials have started an investigation and will check whether the building had the correct permits.
items.title: Apartment building partly collapses in Istanbul; two dead
items.tr: İstanbul Maltepe'de yedi katlı bir apartmanın alt üç katı perşembe sabahı çöktü; iki kişi öldü, üçü çocuk on kişi kurtarıldı ve iki kişi daha aranıyor. Çöküşün nedeni bilinmiyor; yetkililer soruşturma başlattı.

People who use regional buses in the Netherlands should prepare for strikes. The trade unions FNV and CNV will announce their plans on Friday, 9 October. They had given the employers a deadline, and it passed on Wednesday without an agreement.

The conflict is about a collective labour agreement. This is a contract between unions and employers that sets the pay and working conditions for a whole sector. The old agreement ended in June. It covers more than 13,000 workers, mostly bus drivers, at companies such as Arriva, Qbuzz, Keolis and Transdev.

The unions want higher pay, less pressure at work and a special arrangement for older workers. Actions could start from Monday, 12 October. Earlier, the unions talked about one strike day every week until Christmas. The employers' organisation says its offer is good. It says strikes will hurt passengers and make the sector's money problems worse.
items.title: Dutch bus drivers plan strikes after pay talks fail
items.tr: Hollanda'da bölgesel otobüs çalışanlarının sendikaları FNV ve CNV, işverenlerle anlaşma sağlanamayınca grev planlarını cuma günü açıklayacak. Eylemler 12 Ekim'den itibaren başlayabilir; anlaşmazlık 13 binden fazla çalışanın toplu iş sözleşmesiyle ilgili.

China has proposed a candidate to become the next head of the World Health Organization (WHO). Mao Ning, a spokesperson for China's foreign ministry, announced the choice on Thursday, 8 October. The candidate is Song Li, an expert on the health of mothers and children.

The WHO is the United Nations agency for health, based in Geneva. Its current leader, Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus from Ethiopia, must leave in August 2027, because a leader may serve only two terms. The United States left the WHO earlier this year. President Donald Trump has often said that the organisation is too close to China.

Song Li leads the department for women's and children's health at China's National Health Commission. She will compete with six other candidates, proposed by Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Belgium, Spain, Indonesia and Botswana. If she wins, she will be the second Chinese citizen to lead the WHO, after Margaret Chan, who led it from 2007 to 2017.

A committee of the Turkish parliament has approved a proposed law for foreign online accommodation platforms such as Booking.com and Airbnb, Hürriyet Daily News reported on 7 October. The full parliament must still vote, and the law should start on 1 January 2027.

These platforms are websites where travellers reserve hotel rooms or holiday homes. The platform keeps a commission, which is a part of the price. In 2017, a Turkish court stopped the activities of Booking.com, a company from Amsterdam, after Turkish travel agencies complained about unfair competition.

Under the new rules, a platform needs a two-year permit from the Culture and Tourism Ministry. It costs 5 million lira, about 101,000 dollars. The platform must also name a representative in Türkiye. Its commission on sales inside Türkiye may not be higher than 17 percent, and it may not stop hotels from selling rooms in other places. Fines can reach 500,000 lira.

Criminals have bought between 6,000 and 11,000 homes in the Netherlands with false documents in recent years. This estimate comes from a report that is not yet public, the Dutch broadcaster NOS said.

The report was written by the Financial Expertise Centre, a group in which financial supervisors and crime-fighting agencies work together. A mortgage is a bank loan for buying a house. To get one, a buyer must prove a steady income. The fraudsters make false payslips, employer letters and tax forms.

Medy van der Laan, who leads the Dutch banking association NVB, spoke to members of parliament on Wednesday. She said the homes are used for hiding criminal money, illegal renting, exploiting workers and drug crime. Banks and notaries want permission to check a buyer's income with the tax office. The justice ministry has had the report for more than six months. Parliament will discuss the problem next week.

The American space agency NASA made a huge collection of data from its Artemis II Moon mission public on Wednesday, 7 October. It presented the archive at the International Astronautical Congress, a large yearly space meeting, in Antalya, Türkiye. Researchers all over the world can now use it.

Artemis is NASA's programme to send people to the Moon again. In April, four astronauts flew around the Moon in the Artemis II mission and came back safely. They did not land on it. During the flight they travelled 406,771 kilometres from Earth, farther than any humans before them.

The archive is more than 800 gigabytes in size. It contains 12,000 photographs, more than eight hours of unpublished sound recordings of the astronauts, and their handwritten notes and drawings. Each photo now comes with about 300 pieces of extra information that help scientists compare them. NASA wants to land astronauts on the Moon in 2028, for the first time since 1972.

About 425,000 Dutch homes have problems with their foundations, or will soon have them, because of the recent drought. The Dutch public broadcaster NOS reported this on Thursday, 8 October, using numbers from the research institutes Deltares and TNO.

A foundation is the part of a building under the ground that carries its weight. Many Dutch houses stand on clay, which shrinks when it dries out. Then cracks can appear in the walls, and windows and doors may no longer open easily. Other houses stand on wooden poles, which can rot when ground water falls too low.

Repairs can cost tens of thousands of euros per house. A Dutch financial authority estimated the total cost at about 11 billion euros. About 75,000 owners cannot pay for the repairs. Experts expect about 687,000 such homes within 30 years because of climate change. They advise owners to keep the soil around the house wet. A homeowners' group wants help from the government.

The largest penguin colony in the world has become much smaller, a new study shows. The colony lives on Zavodovski Island, a small island near Antarctica. Between 2011 and 2025, the number of breeding penguins there fell from about 1.09 million to 402,000.

The birds are chinstrap penguins, named after the thin black line under their chin. Scientists from the British Antarctic Survey, a British research organisation, led the study. They counted the penguins with drones, photos from planes and satellite pictures. They also put small tracking devices on some birds.

The scientists think climate change is the main reason. Chinstrap penguins mostly eat krill, very small sea animals that look like shrimp. Changes in the ocean mean there is now less krill near the island. The species is still officially listed as "Least Concern", which means it is not in danger. The researchers say experts should check this status again, because the fall was so large and fast.
items.title: World's largest penguin colony loses two-thirds of its birds
items.tr: Antarktika yakınındaki Zavodovski Adası'nda yaşayan dünyanın en büyük penguen kolonisi, 14 yılda kuşlarının yaklaşık üçte ikisini kaybetti. Bilim insanları bunun ana nedeninin iklim değişikliği ve azalan kril olduğunu düşünüyor.

Samsung Electronics said on Thursday, 8 October, that it expects a record profit for July, August and September. The South Korean company estimates its operating profit at 107.4 trillion won, about 80 billion dollars. That is almost nine times as much as in the same period last year.

Samsung is the world's largest maker of memory chips, which store information in computers and phones. Artificial intelligence (AI) companies need huge numbers of these chips for their data centres. There are not enough chips for everyone, so prices have risen sharply. Operating profit is the money a company earns from its normal business, before taxes.

Sales should be 195 trillion won, more than double last year's figure. No South Korean company has ever passed 100 trillion won of profit in three months. But expensive chips also create a problem: Samsung's own phone division must pay more for them. The company will publish its final results at the end of October.

The Dutch government plans to spend 50 million euros on nature around the Port of Rotterdam, the news site DutchNews reported on Thursday, 8 October. One part of the plan is unusual: workers will release wild rabbits into the sand dunes near the port.

The reason is nitrogen. Farms, traffic and factories release nitrogen compounds into the air, and these damage protected nature areas. In 2019 the Council of State, an important Dutch court, ruled that the country's nitrogen policy broke European Union rules on protecting nature. Since then, companies in the port have received almost no permits to build or expand.

The plan says that rabbits help to create dunes that are less sensitive to nitrogen. The number of wild rabbits has fallen sharply because of disease. The aim is that companies in the port can get permits again. Industry in the port has become smaller in recent years, and some chemical factories have closed.

Fenerbahçe's women's basketball team won the FIBA SuperCup Women on Wednesday, 7 October. The Istanbul club beat another Turkish team, Mersin, 79-71. The match took place in Mersin, in the south of Türkiye.

The SuperCup is one match that opens the European season. It is played every year between the winners of Europe's two big club competitions for women. Fenerbahçe won the stronger one, the EuroLeague Women, last season. Mersin won the second one, the EuroCup Women, and played in the SuperCup for the first time.

A basketball match has four parts, called quarters. Mersin led by two points after the first quarter, but Fenerbahçe was ahead 38-32 after two. Later the Istanbul team led by 17 points. Mersin came back to only six points behind with 19 seconds left, but it was too late. Belgian player Emma Meesseman was chosen as the best player of the final. Fenerbahçe also won this cup in 2023 and 2024.

The head of the International Monetary Fund, Kristalina Georgieva, gave a warning about artificial intelligence (AI) on Wednesday, 7 October. Speaking in Singapore, she said the world economy could suffer if investors suddenly lose confidence in AI and take their money out.

The International Monetary Fund, or IMF, is an organisation of about 190 countries that watches the world economy and lends money to states in financial trouble. Companies are now spending huge sums on AI, for example on computer chips and data centres. Georgieva said AI equipment already makes up more than 10 percent of world trade in goods.

She said AI could one day add up to 0.5 percentage points to world growth every year. However, oil costs about 100 dollars a barrel, and government debt worldwide is on the way to becoming larger than everything the world produces in a year. Georgieva said governments cannot keep borrowing more after every crisis.

The United States says it never asked the Netherlands to stop Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado from going home. Secretary of State Marco Rubio, the American foreign minister, called such reports untrue in Athens on Wednesday, 7 October.

Machado won the Nobel Peace Prize last year and left Venezuela through Curaçao to receive it. Curaçao and Aruba are Caribbean islands near Venezuela that are part of the Kingdom of the Netherlands. About two weeks ago, Machado tried to fly to one of these islands and continue by boat. Her plane did not get permission to land.

Aruba's representatives told a Dutch newspaper that the Dutch government decides who may enter. Prime Minister Rob Jetten refuses to give details, saying this could harm cooperation with Venezuela's opposition. News agencies reported earlier that Washington had advised Machado to wait. She wants to return to take part in elections, which she says should be held before the end of the year.

President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan spoke by telephone with Russian President Vladimir Putin on Wednesday, 7 October. According to Türkiye's Communications Directorate, Erdoğan stressed that ships must be able to travel safely in the Black Sea.

The Black Sea lies between Türkiye, Russia, Ukraine and three other countries. Since Russia invaded Ukraine in 2022, the war has spread to these waters, and cargo ships have been hit. In recent days, drones struck two Turkish-owned ships near Bulgaria, and one of them sank.

Türkiye's Chamber of Shipping says more than 200 civilian and commercial ships have been attacked in the Black Sea since the war began, most of them this year. Turkish ships are a target more and more often. Erdoğan also told Putin that Ankara is always ready to help Russia and Ukraine start direct talks. Türkiye has relations with both countries and has hosted talks between them before.

Germany and France have agreed to ask together for softer European Union (EU) rules on pollution from cars. The German business newspaper Handelsblatt reported the agreement between Chancellor Friedrich Merz and President Emmanuel Macron on Wednesday, 7 October.

Under current EU law, new cars must produce no carbon dioxide from 2035. Carbon dioxide, or CO2, is a gas that warms the planet. In practice, this rule would end the sale of new petrol and diesel cars. Last December the European Commission, which proposes EU laws, suggested a cut of 90 percent instead of 100 percent.

Berlin and Paris now want ten more percentage points of freedom, so carmakers could sell more cars with traditional engines after 2035. In exchange, Germany is ready to accept a French demand: government money for electric cars should go mainly to models made in the EU. Members of the European Parliament hope to find a compromise within two weeks.

September was the most expensive month ever for petrol in the Netherlands. A litre of Euro 95, the normal petrol for cars, cost 2.45 euros on average. The news site NL Times and the Dutch news agency ANP reported the numbers on Wednesday, 7 October.

Prices rose after the war in the Middle East began, because oil became more expensive. At the end of September, the recommended price of petrol reached a record of 2.727 euros per litre. Before the war, it was almost 50 cents lower.

The owner of an average petrol car now pays 1,550 euros a year for fuel. That is 321 euros more than a year ago. A survey by the insurance website Autoverzekering.nl shows that 68 percent of drivers have changed their habits. More than a third leave the car at home more often. Many people choose the bicycle instead, especially for short trips. Only 32 percent drive as much as before.
items.title: Record petrol prices change how Dutch people drive

Eighteen ancient objects from the museum in Burdur, a city in south-west Türkiye, are now on show in Copenhagen, the capital of Denmark. They are part of an exhibition at the Glyptotek museum called "The Power of Fashion in the Roman Empire". It opened on 1 October and runs until 29 March 2027.

Two thousand years ago, Anatolia was part of the Roman Empire, so Türkiye has many Roman remains. The exhibition explains how Romans used clothes, jewellery and hairstyles to show who they were and how much power they had. Its most important pieces are large marble statues of emperors' families and rich citizens.

Culture and Tourism Minister Mehmet Nuri Ersoy announced the loan on social media. He said the aim is to show Anatolia's heritage to art lovers around the world. The loan follows the return to Türkiye of an ancient head of the Roman emperor Septimius Severus, which had left the country illegally.

María del Carmen Abascal, an 87-year-old woman known across Spain as Maricarmen, died in a Madrid hospital late on Wednesday, 7 October. Her lawyer, Beatriz Duro, confirmed the news to a Spanish radio station.

Maricarmen had lived in the same flat in Madrid for seventy years. On 23 September, police carried her out on a stretcher because she could not pay a higher rent. Forcing a person to leave a home in this way is called an eviction. The pictures were on television, and huge protests about housing costs followed. Average rents in Spain have almost doubled in ten years.

The property company later agreed that she could return home, but she died before she could go back. A tenants' group in Madrid said the agreement came too late. Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez sent his sympathy to her family. Because of the crisis, he has called an early national election for 29 November.

Türkiye's parliament will receive the Mecca defence agreement for approval within a few days. Ömer Çelik, the spokesman of President Erdoğan's AK Party, said this on Wednesday, 7 October.

The leaders of Türkiye, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan signed the agreement in the Saudi city of Mecca on 7 August 2026. It says that an armed attack on one of the three countries is an attack on all of them. On Monday, the three states decided to send forces to Saudi Arabia quickly, after attacks by the Houthis, an armed group in Yemen. In Türkiye, an international agreement becomes law only after parliament approves it. This step is called ratification.

Sending Turkish soldiers abroad needs a second, separate decision by parliament. A Turkish official told the news agency Reuters that Türkiye has so far given Saudi Arabia military equipment, weapons systems and intelligence. Çelik said the agreement does not replace Türkiye's other alliances and that new members can join.

The Allard Pierson archaeology museum in Amsterdam returned an ancient vase to the Italian island of Sicily on Wednesday, 7 October. The vase was made in the third century BC and shows a wedding scene. Italian officials, including Sicily's heritage minister, came to Amsterdam to receive it.

The museum bought the vase from a Swiss dealer in 1997 at Tefaf, a large art fair in Maastricht. The documents about the object's history, which experts call its provenance, were missing. The seller said the vase had been in a private Swiss collection since before 1970.

In 2016, researchers in Sicily found a roll of film. It showed the vase among objects in the hands of grave robbers in the Sicilian town of Centuripe. The same film had a wedding photo from 1976, so the seller's story could not be true. Dutch law did not force the museum to return the vase, but the museum wanted to take responsibility.

sents.en: The Allard Pierson archaeology museum in Amsterdam returned an ancient vase to the Italian island of Sicily on Wednesday, 7 October.

sents.en: Italian officials, including Sicily's heritage minister, came to Amsterdam to receive it.
sents.tr: Aralarında Sicilya'nın kültürel miras bakanının da bulunduğu İtalyan yetkililer, vazoyu teslim almak için Amsterdam'a geldi.

sents.en: The museum bought the vase from a Swiss dealer in 1997 at Tefaf, a large art fair in Maastricht.
sents.tr: Müze vazoyu 1997'de, Maastricht'teki büyük sanat fuarı Tefaf'ta İsviçreli bir satıcıdan satın aldı.

sents.en: The documents about the object's history, which experts call its provenance, were missing.
sents.tr: Eserin geçmişine dair belgeler, yani uzmanların provenans dediği bilgiler eksikti.

sents.en: The seller said the vase had been in a private Swiss collection since before 1970.
sents.tr: Satıcı, vazonun 1970'ten önce de İsviçre'de özel bir koleksiyonda olduğunu söylemişti.

sents.en: In 2016, researchers in Sicily found a roll of film.
sents.tr: 2016'da Sicilya'daki araştırmacılar bir fotoğraf filmi makarası buldu.

sents.en: It showed the vase among objects in the hands of grave robbers in the Sicilian town of Centuripe.
sents.tr: Filmde vazo, Sicilya'nın Centuripe kasabasındaki mezar soyguncularının elindeki eserler arasında görülüyordu.

sents.en: The same film had a wedding photo from 1976, so the seller's story could not be true.
sents.tr: Aynı filmde 1976 tarihli bir düğün fotoğrafı da vardı; yani satıcının anlattıkları doğru olamazdı.

sents.en: Dutch law did not force the museum to return the vase, but the museum wanted to take responsibility.
sents.tr: Hollanda yasaları müzeyi vazoyu iade etmeye zorlamıyordu, ancak müze sorumluluk almak istedi.

items.title: Amsterdam museum gives ancient vase back to Sicily

A Russian military court sentenced a 68-year-old man on 30 September to six years in a high-security prison camp. Russian media name him as Igor Odintsov. Earlier that month he swam across the border river Nemunas into Lithuania to ask for asylum, but Lithuania sent him back.

Asylum is the protection that a country gives to people who are in danger at home. The case took place in Kaliningrad, a small part of Russia that lies between Lithuania and Poland, far from the rest of the country. Odintsov was already on trial, accused of publicly justifying terrorism. The court said he opposes Russia's government and its war in Ukraine.

He told Lithuanian officials that he was escaping punishment for his posts on social media. Lithuania's border service said his information was inconsistent and that he could be a danger inside the European Union. After prison, Odintsov may not manage websites for three years.

At least 56 wolf cubs were born in the Netherlands this year. BIJ12, the organisation that counts wolves for the Dutch provinces, gave the number on Wednesday, 7 October. There were 37 cubs in Gelderland, 13 in Drenthe and 6 in Utrecht.

A cub is a young wolf. Wolves disappeared from the Netherlands more than a century ago, and the first pair settled here again in 2019. That pair still lives together in the northern Veluwe, a large forest area in Gelderland. The female is at least nine years old, although a wild wolf lives about six years on average.

The real number may be higher, because information from some of the 14 wolf areas is still missing. Last year the count was at least 52. Nobody knows the total number of wolves, because the animals travel far and cross borders. Roads are a danger for them: 17 wolves have died in traffic accidents so far this year.
items.title: Dutch wolves had at least 56 cubs this year
items.tr: Hollanda'da bu yıl en az 56 kurt yavrusu doğdu; çoğu Gelderland eyaletinde. Ülkede toplam kaç kurt yaşadığı bilinmiyor ve bu yıl 17 kurt trafik kazalarında öldü.

The film festival Filmekimi starts in Istanbul on Friday, 9 October, and runs until 18 October. Then it travels to Ankara from 15 to 18 October, and to Izmir and Mersin from 22 to 25 October. It is the 25th time the festival takes place, and its first visit to Mersin.

The name Filmekimi means "film October" in Turkish. Each autumn it shows films that won prizes at the big international festivals, such as Cannes in France and Venice in Italy. The Istanbul Foundation for Culture and Arts organises it. About half of this year's films come from Cannes.

The main film this year is "Fjord" by the Romanian director Cristian Mungiu. It won the Palme d'Or, the top prize at Cannes. There are also films by famous directors such as Pedro Almodóvar and Werner Herzog. Festival director Kerem Ayan says that tickets for the prize winners will sell out first. He advises people to try other films too.
items.title: Filmekimi brings prize-winning films to four Turkish cities
items.tr: 25. kez düzenlenen Filmekimi, Cannes ve Venedik gibi festivallerin ödüllü filmlerini İstanbul, Ankara, İzmir ve ilk kez Mersin'de seyirciyle buluşturuyor. Programın başında Altın Palmiye ödüllü "Fjord" var.

Finland has ordered Google to stop building work at two sites for new data centres. A state agency made the decision on Tuesday, 6 October. The sites are in the areas of Muhos and Kajaani.

A data centre is a large building full of computers that store information and run internet services. Artificial intelligence, or AI, needs many of them. In September, Google said it would invest 13 billion euros in Finland over two years. Before a big project starts, Finnish law demands a study of its effects on nature. This study is called an environmental impact assessment.

The agency suspects that Tuike Finland, the company that represents Google, cut down hundreds of hectares of forest without this study. The work must stop by 23 October at the latest. Google admitted that it did not meet its own standards and promised to follow the agency's instructions. Environment Minister Sari Multala said the projects will probably be late.

People who could not get their money back in Türkiye's fund crisis will start to receive payments on Thursday, 8 October. Vice President Cevdet Yılmaz announced this in parliament in Ankara on Wednesday. The first payments go to 43,643 investors in 17 funds.

An investment fund collects money from many people and invests it for them. In mid-September, some Turkish funds could not pay investors who wanted their money back. The Capital Markets Board, which controls the financial markets, then ordered 131 funds to close. This process is called liquidation. Unlike bank deposits, money in funds has no state guarantee.

Yılmaz said the state will not use public money to cover private losses. Investors will receive money mainly from what each fund owns. More should come from the sale of seized property. If parliament passes a new law, investors in other closed funds may get a first payment of up to 1 million lira this month.

The maker of Chocomel, a popular Dutch chocolate milk, has won a legal fight about the yellow colour of its packs. The Benelux Office for Intellectual Property in The Hague decided this, NL Times reported on Wednesday, 7 October. The other side was a Spanish company, Grupo Cacaolat.

Chocomel belongs to FrieslandCampina, a large Dutch dairy company. A trademark is a name, logo or other sign that only one company may use. The office registers trademarks for Belgium, the Netherlands and Luxembourg. In 2025, Grupo Cacaolat asked the office to register a trademark for its own chocolate milk. Its pack has the same yellow as Chocomel.

FrieslandCampina objected and said the Spanish company would profit from Chocomel's good name. Grupo Cacaolat answered that makers of chocolate milk use yellow to show that a drink contains cocoa. The office agreed with FrieslandCampina. The Dutch company will now ask its rival to change the pack. Grupo Cacaolat has two months to appeal.

A film that a Turkish studio made with artificial intelligence will compete at a film festival in Germany. "A Woman Asleep" is in the main competition of the 36th FilmFestival Cottbus, Türkiye Today reported on Wednesday, 7 October. The report calls it the first full-length AI film in the main competition of an established international festival.

Artificial intelligence, or AI, means computer programs that can create texts, pictures and sounds. The festival takes place in Cottbus, a city in eastern Germany, and is known for films from Eastern Europe. The director is the artist Vikki Bardot, also known as Gizem Avcıoğlu.

The film is 80 minutes long and in English. Bardot trained the AI models herself. A computer copy of her own voice tells the story. She put the film together from about 50,000 separate shots, and the work took two years. The film takes its idea from "A Man Asleep", a 1967 novel by the French writer Georges Perec.

The British car maker Jaguar presented a new electric car at a party in New York this week. The car is called the Type 01EV. It is the first new model since the company changed its whole image two years ago.

Jaguar is a famous old British brand. Many people still love its E-Type sports car from the 1960s. But for years most of its customers were older people, and the company did not win enough young buyers. In 2024, it started again with a new look and an advertisement that showed no car at all. Many people criticised it.

The new car has four doors and is very big: 5.2 metres long and 2,700 kilograms. It can drive 769 kilometres before the battery is empty. In Europe, the price starts at about 140,000 euros. People can order the car from early 2027. The first cars should arrive in Europe in the second half of that year.
items.title: Jaguar presents big electric car for younger, richer buyers
items.tr: İngiliz otomobil üreticisi Jaguar, iki yıl önceki imaj değişikliğinden sonraki ilk yeni modeli olan elektrikli Type 01EV'yi New York'ta tanıttı. 5,2 metre uzunluğundaki otomobilin Avrupa'daki fiyatı yaklaşık 140 bin avrodan başlıyor.

The University of Amsterdam is giving its students fewer essays to write. The university fears that students use artificial intelligence, or AI, to write the texts for them. NL Times reported this on Wednesday, 7 October.

An essay is a longer text in which a student explains ideas about a subject and gives arguments for them. Universities use essays to teach clear thinking and clear writing. Today, AI programs can write such a text in a few seconds. It is very hard to check whether a student or a computer wrote it.

The student organisation ASVA is against the change. Josephine de Haas of ASVA says students have a right to practise these skills. She thinks the university can check for AI texts, just as it checks for copied work. Judith Huigens, who leads the political science programme, calls essays very important. Teachers now give marks during the writing process and not only for the final text.
items.title: Amsterdam university gives fewer essays because of AI
items.tr: Amsterdam Üniversitesi, öğrencilerin metinleri yapay zekâya yazdırmasından endişe ettiği için daha az deneme ödevi veriyor. Öğrenci birliği ASVA ve bazı öğretim üyeleri, yazma becerilerinin gelişmesi için bu ödevlerin şart olduğunu söyleyerek karşı çıkıyor.

Cemil Tugay, the mayor of Izmir, Türkiye's third-largest city, joined the ruling AK Party on Wednesday, 7 October. President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan, who leads the party, gave him the party badge at a meeting in Ankara.

Tugay won the city in March 2024 as the candidate of the CHP, which was then the main opposition party. The AK Party has never won a mayor's election in Izmir, and left-wing parties have governed the city since 1999. In June, a court decision changed the CHP's leadership, and Tugay left the party. Its former leader, Özgür Özel, then founded the New Party.

Tugay is the 105th mayor to move to the AK Party since the 2024 local elections. In August 2025, he said there was not even a one-in-a-million chance that he would join it. The AK Party still does not control Izmir's city council, where the New Party has 91 seats and the AK Party 39.

sents.en: Cemil Tugay, the mayor of Izmir, Türkiye's third-largest city, joined the ruling AK Party on Wednesday, 7 October.
sents.tr: Türkiye'nin üçüncü büyük şehri İzmir'in belediye başkanı Cemil Tugay, 7 Ekim Çarşamba günü iktidardaki AK Parti'ye katıldı.

sents.en: President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan, who leads the party, gave him the party badge at a meeting in Ankara.
sents.tr: Partinin genel başkanı olan Cumhurbaşkanı Recep Tayyip Erdoğan, Ankara'daki bir toplantıda ona parti rozetini taktı.

sents.en: Tugay won the city in March 2024 as the candidate of the CHP, which was then the main opposition party.
sents.tr: Tugay şehri Mart 2024'te, o dönemde ana muhalefet partisi olan CHP'nin adayı olarak kazanmıştı.

sents.en: The AK Party has never won a mayor's election in Izmir, and left-wing parties have governed the city since 1999.
sents.tr: AK Parti İzmir'de bugüne kadar hiç belediye başkanlığı seçimi kazanamadı; şehri 1999'dan beri sol partiler yönetiyor.

sents.en: In June, a court decision changed the CHP's leadership, and Tugay left the party.
sents.tr: Haziran ayında bir mahkeme kararı CHP'nin yönetimini değiştirdi ve Tugay partiden ayrıldı.

sents.en: Its former leader, Özgür Özel, then founded the New Party.
sents.tr: Partinin eski lideri Özgür Özel de ardından Yeni Parti'yi kurdu.

sents.en: Tugay is the 105th mayor to move to the AK Party since the 2024 local elections.
sents.tr: Tugay, 2024 yerel seçimlerinden bu yana AK Parti'ye geçen 105. belediye başkanı oldu.

sents.en: In August 2025, he said there was not even a one-in-a-million chance that he would join it.
sents.tr: Ağustos 2025'te, bu partiye katılma ihtimalinin milyonda bir bile olmadığını söylemişti.

sents.en: The AK Party still does not control Izmir's city council, where the New Party has 91 seats and the AK Party 39.
sents.tr: AK Parti, İzmir'in belediye meclisinde hâlâ çoğunluğa sahip değil; mecliste Yeni Parti'nin 91, AK Parti'nin 39 sandalyesi var.

items.title: Izmir's mayor leaves the opposition and joins Erdoğan's party
items.tr: İzmir Büyükşehir Belediye Başkanı Cemil Tugay, 7 Ekim'de Ankara'da AK Parti'ye katıldı. Tugay, 2024 yerel seçimlerinden bu yana AK Parti'ye geçen 105. belediye başkanı oldu.

Hungary is ready to stop blocking the next step in Ukraine's talks to join the European Union, Euronews reported on Wednesday, 7 October. There is one condition: next week, Ukraine's parliament must pass a law on the rights of minorities.

A country that wants to join the EU must negotiate on many subjects, organised in groups called clusters. All 27 member countries must agree to open a cluster, so one country can block it. This is called a veto. Hungary's former prime minister, Viktor Orbán, often used his veto against Ukraine. Péter Magyar, prime minister since May, promised a more practical approach.

Hungary wants stronger education and cultural rights for the Hungarian minority in Transcarpathia, a region in western Ukraine. If the law passes, EU ministers plan to open two clusters, on the internal market and competitiveness. At the same time, the EU is expected to pay Hungary 4.2 billion euros that it had held back because of corruption worries.

sents.en: Hungary is ready to stop blocking the next step in Ukraine's talks to join the European Union, Euronews reported on Wednesday, 7 October.
sents.tr: Euronews'un 7 Ekim Çarşamba günü bildirdiğine göre Macaristan, Ukrayna'nın Avrupa Birliği'ne katılım görüşmelerindeki bir sonraki adımı engellemekten vazgeçmeye hazır.

sents.en: There is one condition: next week, Ukraine's parliament must pass a law on the rights of minorities.
sents.tr: Tek bir şart var: Ukrayna meclisi gelecek hafta azınlık haklarıyla ilgili bir yasayı kabul etmeli.

sents.en: A country that wants to join the EU must negotiate on many subjects, organised in groups called clusters.
sents.tr: AB'ye katılmak isteyen bir ülke, "küme" denen gruplar hâlinde düzenlenmiş birçok konuda müzakere yürütmek zorundadır.

sents.en: All 27 member countries must agree to open a cluster, so one country can block it.
sents.tr: Bir kümenin açılması için 27 üye ülkenin hepsinin onay vermesi gerekir; bu yüzden tek bir ülke bunu engelleyebilir.

sents.en: This is called a veto.
sents.tr: Buna veto denir.

sents.en: Hungary's former prime minister, Viktor Orbán, often used his veto against Ukraine.
sents.tr: Macaristan'ın eski başbakanı Viktor Orbán, vetosunu Ukrayna'ya karşı sık sık kullandı.

sents.en: Péter Magyar, prime minister since May, promised a more practical approach.
sents.tr: Mayıs ayından beri başbakan olan Péter Magyar ise daha pragmatik bir yaklaşım sözü verdi.

sents.en: Hungary wants stronger education and cultural rights for the Hungarian minority in Transcarpathia, a region in western Ukraine.
sents.tr: Macaristan, Ukrayna'nın batısındaki bir bölge olan Transkarpatya'daki Macar azınlık için eğitim ve kültür alanında daha güçlü haklar istiyor.

sents.en: If the law passes, EU ministers plan to open two clusters, on the internal market and competitiveness.
sents.tr: Yasa kabul edilirse AB bakanları iç pazar ve rekabet gücü konularındaki iki kümeyi açmayı planlıyor.

sents.en: At the same time, the EU is expected to pay Hungary 4.2 billion euros that it had held back because of corruption worries.
sents.tr: Aynı zamanda AB'nin, yolsuzluk endişeleri nedeniyle beklettiği 4,2 milyar avroyu Macaristan'a ödemesi bekleniyor.

Russia has asked Vietnam to rent it passenger planes together with their crews and maintenance, Euronews reported on Wednesday, 7 October. Transport Minister Andrei Nikitin announced the proposal. Such a deal is called a "wet lease".

Before Russia invaded Ukraine in February 2022, about 850 of its 900 commercial planes were Boeing or Airbus models, mostly rented from foreign companies. After the invasion, Western sanctions banned the sale of planes and spare parts to Russia. Russia then passed a law that let its airlines keep more than 400 rented planes.

Airlines now take parts from some planes to repair others. About 130 of the 673 planes of Russia's 11 largest airlines cannot fly now, almost one in five and twice the normal share. Vietnam's main airline uses only Airbus and Boeing planes, so helping Russia could bring sanctions on it too. Russian officials are also discussing a fee of 500 roubles on domestic flights to pay for Russian-made planes.

sents.en: Russia has asked Vietnam to rent it passenger planes together with their crews and maintenance, Euronews reported on Wednesday, 7 October.
sents.tr: Euronews'un 7 Ekim Çarşamba günü bildirdiğine göre Rusya, Vietnam'dan kendisine mürettebatı ve bakımıyla birlikte yolcu uçağı kiralamasını istedi.

sents.en: Transport Minister Andrei Nikitin announced the proposal.
sents.tr: Teklifi Ulaştırma Bakanı Andrey Nikitin duyurdu.

sents.tr: Böyle bir anlaşmaya "wet lease" (mürettebatlı kiralama) denir.

Dirk Gotink, a member of the European Parliament, has left the Dutch party NSC, DutchNews reported on Wednesday, 7 October. He was the party's last elected representative in any parliament. Gotink, 45, will stay there as an independent member.

Pieter Omtzigt, a well-known member of parliament, founded NSC (New Social Contract) in August 2023. A few months later, the party won 20 of the 150 seats in the Dutch parliament. It then joined a government with Geert Wilders's far-right PVV and lost support. Omtzigt left politics in 2025 because of health problems. In the election of October 2025, NSC lost all its seats.

Gotink left because NSC invited Mona Keijzer to speak at a party conference in Breda. Keijzer leads Project 2029, a movement that is very critical of the EU. The party's board said she is only a guest speaker, but Gotink sees a clear political choice. He wrote that the EU is necessary for Dutch freedom and prosperity.

The Dutch asylum minister, Bart van den Brink, presented a new bill on Wednesday, 7 October. Under this plan, people whose asylum request was refused and who actively block their return can get up to six months in prison.

Asylum is protection that a country gives to people who are not safe in their own country. When the Netherlands refuses a request, the person must leave. If the state sends the person away, this is called deportation. Some people make this difficult: they give a false name or refuse to cooperate.

On the same day, COA, the agency that gives asylum seekers a place to sleep, said its centres are too full. It is short of hundreds of places, also in Ter Apel, the village where asylum seekers first register. COA says the reason is not more arrivals. People stay longer because decisions are slow and refugees who may stay cannot find homes. Parliament must still vote on the bill.
items.title: Dutch plan: prison for people who block their deportation
items.tr: Hollanda'nın sığınma bakanı, sığınma başvurusu reddedilen ve sınır dışı edilmesini bilerek engelleyen kişilere altı aya kadar hapis cezası öngören bir yasa tasarısı sundu. Aynı gün COA, sığınmacı merkezlerinde yüzlerce yer eksiği olduğunu açıkladı.

People aged 21 to 30 made 57% of the purchases of games and digital content in Türkiye in September. The gaming marketplace Oyunfor published these numbers, and Türkiye Today reported them on Wednesday, 7 October.

Oyunfor is an online shop where players buy gift cards and items for use inside games. Many popular games are free to play, but players pay for extras such as new clothes for their characters. These are called in-game purchases. The numbers show only what this shop's own customers bought, so they do not describe the whole market.

People over 30 made 38% of the purchases, and those aged 18 to 21 only 5%. Men made 55% and women 45%. Mobile phones were the most used device with 41%, followed by computers with 33% and consoles with 26%. Players spent the most inside the shooting game Counter-Strike 2, followed by PUBG Mobile and Valorant. Most purchases came from Istanbul, Ankara and Antalya.
items.title: People in their twenties buy most games in Türkiye
items.tr: Oyun satış platformu Oyunfor'un eylül ayı verilerine göre Türkiye'de oyun ve dijital içerik alımlarının %57'sini 21-30 yaş arasındakiler yaptı. Oyun içi harcamalarda ilk sırada Counter-Strike 2 yer aldı.

Lionel Messi played his last match for Argentina's national football team on Tuesday evening, 6 October. Argentina beat Benin 3-0 in a friendly match, a game that is not part of any competition, at the Monumental Stadium in Buenos Aires. More than 85,000 fans watched.

Messi is 39, and many people call him one of the best footballers in history. He joined Argentina's senior team in 2005. For years he lost important finals. Later he won the Copa América, the championship of South America, in 2021 and 2024, and the World Cup in 2022. He announced the end of his international career in August, after Argentina lost this summer's World Cup final to Spain.

In his last game he scored a penalty and helped his teammates to score the other two goals. He leaves with 208 matches and 126 goals, both records for Argentina. "It was a huge source of pride for me to wear this shirt," he said.
items.title: Messi plays his last match for Argentina
items.tr: Lionel Messi, Buenos Aires'te Benin'i 3-0 yendikleri hazırlık maçıyla Arjantin Millî Takımı'na veda etti. 39 yaşındaki yıldız, 208 maç ve 126 golle ülkesinin rekorlarını elinde tutuyor.

Australia's highest court stopped the expansion of a large coal mine on Wednesday, 7 October. Three of the High Court's five judges decided that the Mount Pleasant mine in the state of New South Wales may not grow as planned.

The mine's owner, Mach Energy, wanted to keep it open more than 20 years longer, until 2048, and to produce almost twice as much coal each year. A state planning office had approved this. Two retired science teachers, Wendy Wales and Tony Lonergan, went to court against the plan. Burning coal releases greenhouse gases, which are gases that make the planet warmer.

The judges said the planning office had not made sure that these gases would be kept as low as possible. Climate groups say officials across the country must now consider climate damage before they approve coal or gas projects. Australia is one of the world's biggest sellers of coal. Mach Energy said it was disappointed.

sents.en: Australia's highest court stopped the expansion of a large coal mine on Wednesday, 7 October.
sents.tr: Avustralya'nın en yüksek mahkemesi 7 Ekim Çarşamba günü büyük bir kömür madeninin genişletilmesini durdurdu.

About 250,000 former students in the Netherlands will pay more interest on their student loans from 2027. The Dutch news agency ANP reported the new rates on Wednesday, 7 October.

Dutch students can borrow money from the government to pay for their studies and living costs. After they finish, they pay back the loan over many years. People who borrowed before 2015 have 15 years; later students have up to 35 years. The interest, which is the extra money you pay for borrowing, stays the same for five years. After that it is calculated again.

For the 15-year group, the rate rises by almost one percentage point to 3.28 percent. For the 35-year group it goes up to 2.7 percent. The change affects only people whose five-year period ends this year, and students who were still borrowing in 2026. Student organisations say borrowers may pay thousands of euros more, and they want a maximum rate.
items.title: Interest on Dutch student loans will rise in 2027
items.tr: Hollanda'da yaklaşık 250 bin eski öğrencinin öğrenim kredisi faizi 2027'de yükselecek; 15 yıllık kredilerde oran yüzde 3,28'e çıkıyor. Öğrenci örgütleri faize üst sınır getirilmesini istiyor.

Cigarettes sold in Türkiye release more harmful particles than the same brands sold in Germany. Researchers from Goethe University Frankfurt in Germany found this in a new study, the news site Türkiye Today reported this week.

The scientists measured "particulate matter". These are very small pieces of solid material in smoke or dirty air. They can go deep into the lungs, and doctors link them to heart and lung disease. Both countries limit tar, nicotine and carbon monoxide in cigarettes, but neither has rules for these particles.

The team tested 11 products from Türkiye and four from Germany. A machine smoked them in a closed room about as big as the inside of a small car. The Turkish versions produced between 3.6 and 51 percent more particles. A Turkish tobacco expert said companies prepare cigarettes differently for each country's rules. The study did not test whether this explains the difference.

sents.en: Cigarettes sold in Türkiye release more harmful particles than the same brands sold in Germany.
sents.tr: Türkiye'de satılan sigaralar, Almanya'da satılan aynı markalara göre daha fazla zararlı parçacık yayıyor.
