The next big United Nations climate meeting, called COP31, will start on 9 November in Antalya, on Türkiye's Mediterranean coast. Experts expect only small steps from it.

COP means "Conference of the Parties". It is a yearly meeting where almost all countries discuss how to slow climate change. Türkiye is the host this year, and Australia leads the negotiations. It comes after a year of deadly heat waves and fires in Europe and terrible floods in Nepal.

There are more than 100 topics on the list, but many are technical. Countries are not expected to make new binding promises to use less oil, gas and coal. Türkiye proposes a voluntary goal: electricity should cover 35 percent of the world's energy use by 2035, compared with about 20 percent today. Critics note that the plan does not say how the electricity is made; about one third still comes from coal.

sents.en: The next big United Nations climate meeting, called COP31, will start on 9 November in Antalya, on Türkiye's Mediterranean coast.
sents.tr: Birleşmiş Milletler'in COP31 adlı bir sonraki büyük iklim toplantısı 9 Kasım'da Türkiye'nin Akdeniz kıyısındaki Antalya'da başlayacak.

sents.en: Experts expect only small steps from it.
sents.tr: Uzmanlar toplantıdan yalnızca küçük adımlar bekliyor.

sents.en: COP means "Conference of the Parties".
sents.tr: COP, ‘Taraflar Konferansı’ anlamına gelir.

sents.en: It is a yearly meeting where almost all countries discuss how to slow climate change.
sents.tr: Neredeyse tüm ülkelerin iklim değişikliğini nasıl yavaşlatacaklarını görüştüğü yıllık bir toplantıdır.

sents.en: Türkiye is the host this year, and Australia leads the negotiations.
sents.tr: Bu yıl ev sahibi Türkiye, müzakereleri ise Avustralya yürütüyor.

sents.en: It comes after a year of deadly heat waves and fires in Europe and terrible floods in Nepal.
sents.tr: Toplantı, Avrupa'da ölümcül sıcak hava dalgaları ve yangınların, Nepal'de de korkunç sellerin yaşandığı bir yılın ardından geliyor.

sents.en: There are more than 100 topics on the list, but many are technical.
sents.tr: Listede 100'den fazla konu var, ama birçoğu teknik.

sents.en: Countries are not expected to make new binding promises to use less oil, gas and coal.
sents.tr: Ülkelerin daha az petrol, doğal gaz ve kömür kullanmak için yeni bağlayıcı sözler vermesi beklenmiyor.

sents.en: Türkiye proposes a voluntary goal: electricity should cover 35 percent of the world's energy use by 2035, compared with about 20 percent today.
sents.tr: Türkiye gönüllü bir hedef öneriyor: 2035'e kadar elektrik, bugünkü yaklaşık yüzde 20'ye kıyasla, dünyanın enerji kullanımının yüzde 35'ini karşılamalı.

sents.en: Critics note that the plan does not say how the electricity is made; about one third still comes from coal.
sents.tr: Eleştirenler, planın elektriğin nasıl üretileceğini söylemediğine dikkat çekiyor; elektriğin yaklaşık üçte biri hâlâ kömürden geliyor.

items.title: Türkiye prepares to host world climate meeting in Antalya
items.tr: BM iklim zirvesi COP31, 9 Kasım'da Antalya'da başlayacak; uzmanlar bu yıl yalnızca küçük adımlar bekliyor. Türkiye, elektriğin dünya enerji tüketimindeki payını 2035'e kadar yüzde 35'e çıkarmayı öneriyor.

Videos of mice running through the departure halls of Schiphol airport are spreading on social media this week, and many travellers are angry. One passenger wrote on X on 5 October, after two hours at the airport, that mice were running around the departure area. The passenger called it disgusting.

Schiphol, near Amsterdam, is the largest airport in the Netherlands and one of the busiest in Europe. Mice are not a new problem there: the airport is very large, lies next to open fields and has many restaurants. In September 2022, passengers who had to sleep on the floor because of long delays also complained about mice.

This summer travellers saw mice in a KLM lounge, in the food halls and near gates with food shops. The airport says the summer was very busy, so more food waste was left behind. Last year it said a pest control company checks the buildings every day.
items.title: Videos of mice at Schiphol airport anger travellers
items.tr: Schiphol Havalimanı'nın giden yolcu salonlarında koşan farelerin videoları sosyal medyada yayıldı ve yolcuları kızdırdı. Havalimanı, yoğun geçen yazın daha fazla yemek atığına yol açtığını söylüyor.

The 2026 Nobel Prize in Chemistry goes to two scientists: Henri Kagan from France and Kenso Soai from Japan. The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences announced the winners in Stockholm on Wednesday, 7 October.

Many molecules exist in two forms that are mirror images of each other, like a left hand and a right hand. In a medicine, for example, one form may help the patient while the other does nothing or even causes harm. Living things use only one form of many important molecules, and scientists have long asked why.

Kagan found ways to control chemical reactions so that they make much more of one form than of the other. Soai later designed a reaction that produces only one form. Their work is useful for making medicines, perfumes and new materials. It also helps to explain why the molecules of life are one-sided. The two men will share 12 million Swedish kronor, about 1.2 million dollars.

From 2029, people in the Netherlands who replace their old central heating boiler must install a smart hybrid heat pump. Housing minister Elanor Boekholt-O'Sullivan announced the rule on Wednesday, 7 October.

Most Dutch homes are heated by a boiler that burns natural gas. A heat pump takes warmth from the air outside and uses electricity to heat the house. A hybrid heat pump works together with a gas boiler. The smart type can change to gas when very many people are using electricity, so the busy Dutch power network does not get too full. The government wants all homes to stop using natural gas by 2050.

A hybrid heat pump costs about 8,000 euros, while a normal boiler costs about 2,000 euros. The government will pay 2,000 euros per home, and people who cannot pay the rest may get a loan without interest. The rule does not apply to apartments or historic buildings. There are not enough installers yet.
items.title: Dutch homes must get hybrid heat pumps from 2029

Visitors to the Museum of Innocence in Istanbul have started to leave their own small things there, such as cigarettes, earrings and notes. They put them in the drawers under the display cases, Türkiye Today reported on 7 October. Museum manager Gizem Dündar says visitors become part of the museum in this way.

The writer Orhan Pamuk, who won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 2006, created the museum. It belongs to his 2008 novel of the same name. In the story, a rich man called Kemal loves Füsun, a poorer distant relative, and collects everyday objects that remind him of her. Pamuk planned the book and the museum together and bought most of the objects himself in Istanbul's antique shops. It opened in 2012.

One display holds 4,213 cigarette ends. In February 2026, Netflix released a nine-part series based on the novel, and the number of visitors rose sharply. Now about 150 people come every day.
items.title: Visitors leave their own memories at Pamuk's Istanbul museum
items.tr: İstanbul'daki Masumiyet Müzesi'nde ziyaretçiler vitrinlerin altındaki çekmecelere kendi küçük eşyalarını bırakmaya başladı. Orhan Pamuk'un romanına dayanan müze, Netflix dizisinden sonra daha çok ziyaretçi çekiyor.

Kosovo's parliament has elected Justina Shiroka-Pula as the country's new president. The vote came just in time. The Constitutional Court had set 6 October as the final date. Without a president, Kosovo would have had to hold a new general election.

Kosovo is a small country in south-east Europe that declared independence from Serbia in 2008. Its president is chosen by the 120 members of parliament, not directly by the people, and has mostly a symbolic role. The parties argued about the job for months. In the end, Prime Minister Albin Kurti's party made a deal with the opposition party PDK. As part of the deal, parliament changed the law on a special court in The Hague that judges former Kosovo fighters for war crimes.

Shiroka-Pula is 73 and an economist. She leads Kosovo's Academy of Sciences and Arts. She received 81 votes, only one more than she needed. "I will be the president of all citizens," she said.

Fatih Karahan, the head of Türkiye's central bank, says the recent crisis in investment funds has had only a limited effect on the real economy. He spoke to the Planning and Budget Commission of parliament, Türkiye Today reported on 7 October.

An investment fund collects money from many people and invests it for them. In the middle of September, some Turkish funds could not pay back investors who wanted their money. The Capital Markets Board, which controls the financial markets, then ordered 131 funds from seven companies to close. About 456,000 people had money in them, and the funds held more than 19 billion dollars.

Karahan said companies owned only a small part of these funds, and the links between the funds and the banks are weak. The central bank has made it easier for banks to borrow cash. He added that lira deposits in banks have grown and that trust in the lira is still strong.

The Dutch state is going to reduce its share in the bank ABN Amro from 20.7 percent to 10.5 percent. NLFI, the organisation that manages the government's shares in financial companies, announced the plan on Wednesday, 7 October.

ABN Amro is one of the largest banks in the Netherlands. During the world financial crisis of 2008, the government bought the bank to stop it from collapsing. In 2015 the bank returned to the stock exchange, the market where company shares are bought and sold. Since then, the state has sold its shares step by step.

This is the fifth sale of this kind. The last one ended in July and brought the state about 2.5 billion euros. On Tuesday the whole bank was worth about 34.5 billion euros. The bank's chief executive, Marguerite Bérard, welcomed the decision. ABN Amro is also cutting more than 5,000 jobs to increase its profits.

A group of climbers has made a new route to a little-known natural wonder in eastern Türkiye, Türkiye Today reported on 7 October. It is a group of stone columns near the village of Karagüney, in the Kağızman district of Kars province. They stand about 1,890 metres above sea level.

The columns are made of basalt, a dark rock that forms when lava cools and becomes hard. Lava is the hot liquid rock that comes out of a volcano. Here the rock formed columns with five or six sides, so they look very regular. They are 6 to 7 million years old. Such columns exist in only a small number of places in the world.

Ali Öztürk of the Iğdır Mountain Safari Club visited the place with a group of ten people. They studied the area and created a new route to reach it. Öztürk said the columns have a remarkable structure.
items.title: Climbers open a route to rare stone columns in Kars
items.tr: Iğdır Dağ Safari Kulübü'nden on kişilik bir grup, Kars'ın Kağızman ilçesindeki Karagüney köyü yakınında bulunan 6-7 milyon yıllık bazalt sütunlarına yeni bir rota açtı. Beş ve altı kenarlı bu sütunlar dünyada az sayıda yerde görülüyor.

The British composer George Fenton died on Monday, 5 October, at the age of 76. His family announced the news and said his death was unexpected. A composer is a person who writes music.

Fenton wrote music for films and television for more than fifty years. Many people know his work from the nature programmes of David Attenborough, the famous British presenter: "The Blue Planet", "Planet Earth" and "Frozen Planet". He also wrote the music for well-known films such as "Gandhi", "Dangerous Liaisons" and "Groundhog Day". For many years he worked with the British director Ken Loach, for example on "I, Daniel Blake".

Fenton was nominated five times for an Oscar, the most famous film prize. He won two Emmy awards, which are American television prizes, and three BAFTAs, the main British film and television prizes. His last film music, for "Up Against It", had its first showing at the Toronto film festival in September.
items.title: George Fenton, composer of "Planet Earth" music, dies at 76
items.tr: "Planet Earth" ve "The Blue Planet" gibi David Attenborough belgesellerinin ve "Gandhi" filminin müziklerini yazan İngiliz besteci George Fenton 76 yaşında beklenmedik şekilde hayatını kaybetti. Fenton beş kez Oscar'a aday gösterilmişti.

Skytree, a climate technology company from Amsterdam, has received a loan of €1 million from Invest International, an investor of the Dutch state. NL Times reported this on Tuesday, 6 October. The company wants to build an installation in Iceland that takes carbon dioxide (CO2) out of the air.

CO2 is a gas that is released when people burn oil, gas or coal. It collects in the air and makes the Earth warmer. Removing it from the air with machines is called direct air capture. Skytree has worked on this technology for ten years. In Iceland, the installation will use geothermal energy, which is heat from deep under the ground.

It will be Skytree's first installation abroad and should work by 2028. The loan does not pay for the building. It covers the technical design, permits, studies of the site and contracts with buyers. Companies can use the captured CO2 in greenhouses, in the food industry and for cleaner fuels.

Lithuania's parliament took a first step on Tuesday, 6 October, to remove a ban on nuclear weapons from the country's constitution. In the capital, Vilnius, 106 members voted for the change and 18 voted against it.

Lithuania is a small country on the Baltic Sea. It borders Belarus and Kaliningrad, a part of Russia, and it has been a member of NATO, the Western military alliance, since 2004. Article 137 of its constitution forbids weapons of mass destruction, such as nuclear bombs, and foreign military bases on its territory. So planes or ships of its allies cannot enter the country with nuclear weapons.

Supporters say Lithuania should not be less protected than neighbours such as Latvia, Estonia and Poland, which have no such rule. Parliament must vote again after three months, and at least 94 of the 141 members must agree. The second vote is planned for 12 January. Russia's government warned that the step could increase tensions.

sents.en: Lithuania's parliament took a first step on Tuesday, 6 October, to remove a ban on nuclear weapons from the country's constitution.

The Dutch government meets employers and trade unions again on Wednesday, 7 October, to talk about social security. Social security is the system of payments from the state to people who cannot work or who are retired.

The government wanted to save money on three payments: the state pension (AOW), the benefit for people who cannot work because of illness or disability (WIA), and the unemployment benefit (WW). After months of protests and strikes, it took all these cuts out of next year's budget. In the Netherlands, the government often negotiates with employers and unions. People call this system the "polder".

Without the cuts, the budget has a gap of €2.4 billion. All sides agree that the population is getting older and that artificial intelligence may destroy jobs, but they do not agree on solutions. Finance Minister Eelco Heinen said reforms must happen "one way or another". If the talks fail, the government must save money elsewhere.

Since 2007, higher temperatures, and not a lack of rain or snow, have been the main cause of "snow drought" in Türkiye. Researchers from Istanbul Technical University report this in the Hydrological Sciences Journal, Türkiye Today wrote on 7 October. They studied the years 1990 to 2024.

A snow drought is a winter with much less snow on the ground than normal. It can happen because little precipitation (rain or snow) falls, or because warm weather makes it fall as rain. Mountain snow works like a natural water tank. It melts in spring and fills rivers and dams.

The team looked at 15 river basins, areas whose water flows into one river. There, melted snow provides about 45% of the river water. In years that were both warm and dry, rivers carried about 36% less water. Researcher Abdullah Akbaş said the question is no longer only how much water there is, but also when it is available.

Websites of many Dutch political parties follow their visitors without permission. The magazine Vrij Nederland and the Internet Cleanup Foundation found this, NL Times reported on Tuesday, 6 October. The researchers checked 6,168 web addresses and found illegal tracking cookies on more than 40 sites.

A cookie is a small file that a website puts on your computer. Tracking cookies record what you look at, often for advertising companies. The European privacy law, known as GDPR, says that a website must ask for your permission first. On the party sites, personal information, including political preferences, went to American technology companies such as Google and YouTube.

They belong to national parties, youth groups and regional branches. The PVV, the party of Geert Wilders, had the most, with 28 sites. The ChristenUnie had three, and FVD and JA21 two each. Felienne Hermans, a professor of computer science in Amsterdam, called it negligence. She said parties should set the right example.

Libya's House of Representatives, the parliament in the east of the country, chose a new speaker on Tuesday, 6 October. Al-Salhin Abdelnabi al-Obeidi replaces Aguila Saleh, who had led the parliament for 12 years. A speaker is the person who leads the meetings of a parliament.

Libya is a large country in North Africa. Since the fall of its ruler Muammar Gaddafi in 2011, it has been divided. A government in the capital, Tripoli, is recognised by the United Nations. A rival administration in the east has the support of the military commander Khalifa Haftar. Saleh was known as Haftar's ally.

One day earlier, 98 members approved a new rule: a speaker may serve only one term of 12 months. Members complained that the old leadership decided things without asking them. Saleh rejects the changes and says they have no legal effect. An agreement between the rival sides in August aims at national elections within two years.

Trabzon ice cream now has a geographical indication, Türkiye Today reported on 7 October. The Turkish Patent and Trademark Office registered it. It is the tenth food from Trabzon, a city on Türkiye's Black Sea coast, with this status.

A geographical indication is an official label for a product that is connected to one place and made in a traditional way. Trabzon ice cream contains full-fat cow's milk, sugar and salep, a flour made from the roots of orchids. Makers cook the mixture for at least eight hours. This long cooking gives the ice cream a yellowish colour.

The city's Chamber of Commerce and Industry applied for the label. Its president, Erkut Çelebi, wants to bring the city's many ice creams together under one name and create a world brand. Producers will now follow a common recipe. The city also hopes to become a UNESCO City of Gastronomy, a title for places with a special food culture.

Carles Puigdemont, the former president of the Spanish region of Catalonia, can return to Spain without being arrested. On Tuesday, 6 October, a judge of Spain's Supreme Court cancelled the arrest warrant against him, Al Jazeera reported. Puigdemont has lived in Belgium since 2017.

Catalonia is a region in the north-east of Spain, around the city of Barcelona. In October 2017, Puigdemont's regional government held a referendum, a public vote, on independence. Spain's courts had forbidden it. He then left the country. In 2024, Spain passed an amnesty law. An amnesty means that the state no longer punishes people for certain past acts. But judges did not apply it to one accusation against him, the misuse of public money.

Now the Constitutional Court has decided that the amnesty covers this accusation too. The date of his return is not known yet. An official of his party, Junts, said he will probably not be a candidate in November's early national election.

The Netherlands must examine more than 140,000 asylum requests from Ukrainian refugees that it had put aside. This follows from a ruling of the EU's highest court, the Court of Justice, the broadcaster NOS reported on Tuesday, 6 October.

After Russia invaded Ukraine in February 2022, the EU started a special rule, the Temporary Protection Directive. It gives Ukrainians the right to housing, health care, work and education. Asylum is individual protection for a person who is not safe at home, and it gives more certainty. Because Ukrainians already had temporary protection, the Dutch immigration service IND did not handle their requests. The court says a country may not postpone them without a time limit.

The asylum minister, Van den Brink, said the IND does not have enough staff for so many files. It will first deal with new asylum seekers, then with about 50,000 waiting cases, and last with the Ukrainians. The temporary protection ends on 4 March 2028.

A new film about Sam Altman, the head of the artificial intelligence company OpenAI, had its first showing on 5 October at the New York Film Festival. It is called "Artificial". The Italian director Luca Guadagnino made it, and the actor Andrew Garfield plays Altman.

OpenAI makes ChatGPT, a program that answers questions. The film tells the story of a few dramatic days in November 2023. The company's board, the group of people who supervise the managers, dismissed Altman. Most employees signed a letter of protest, and he returned to his job a few days later.

The film cost 40 million dollars. The studio Amazon MGM supported it at first but left the project after it signed a large partnership with OpenAI. Another company, Neon, then took over. Early reviews are positive, and people already talk about Oscar nominations for the actors. Garfield said he admired Altman at first but changed his opinion while he prepared for the role.

sents.en: A new film about Sam Altman, the head of the artificial intelligence company OpenAI, had its first showing on 5 October at the New York Film Festival.
sents.tr: Yapay zekâ şirketi OpenAI'ın başındaki Sam Altman'ı anlatan yeni bir film, ilk gösterimini 5 Ekim'de New York Film Festivali'nde yaptı.

sents.en: It is called "Artificial".
sents.tr: Filmin adı ‘Artificial’.

sents.en: The Italian director Luca Guadagnino made it, and the actor Andrew Garfield plays Altman.
sents.tr: Filmi İtalyan yönetmen Luca Guadagnino çekti; Altman'ı oyuncu Andrew Garfield canlandırıyor.

sents.en: OpenAI makes ChatGPT, a program that answers questions.
sents.tr: OpenAI, sorulara cevap veren bir program olan ChatGPT'yi üretiyor.

sents.en: The film tells the story of a few dramatic days in November 2023.
sents.tr: Film, Kasım 2023'teki birkaç dramatik günün hikâyesini anlatıyor.

sents.en: The company's board, the group of people who supervise the managers, dismissed Altman.
sents.tr: Şirketin yönetim kurulu, yani yöneticileri denetleyen kişilerden oluşan grup, Altman'ı görevden aldı.

sents.en: Most employees signed a letter of protest, and he returned to his job a few days later.
sents.tr: Çalışanların çoğu bir protesto mektubu imzaladı ve Altman birkaç gün sonra görevine döndü.

sents.en: The film cost 40 million dollars.
sents.tr: Film 40 milyon dolara mal oldu.

sents.en: The studio Amazon MGM supported it at first but left the project after it signed a large partnership with OpenAI.
sents.tr: Amazon MGM stüdyosu başta filmi destekledi, ama OpenAI ile büyük bir ortaklık anlaşması imzaladıktan sonra projeden çekildi.

sents.en: Another company, Neon, then took over.
sents.tr: Bunun üzerine başka bir şirket, Neon, projeyi devraldı.

sents.en: Early reviews are positive, and people already talk about Oscar nominations for the actors.
sents.tr: İlk eleştiriler olumlu ve oyuncular için şimdiden Oscar adaylıklarından söz ediliyor.

sents.en: Garfield said he admired Altman at first but changed his opinion while he prepared for the role.
sents.tr: Garfield, başta Altman'a hayranlık duyduğunu, ama role hazırlanırken fikrinin değiştiğini söyledi.

items.title: Film about OpenAI boss Sam Altman opens in New York
items.tr: OpenAI'ın patronu Sam Altman'ın Kasım 2023'te görevden alınıp birkaç gün sonra geri dönmesini anlatan "Artificial" filmi New York Film Festivali'nde ilk kez gösterildi. Luca Guadagnino'nun yönettiği filmde Altman'ı Andrew Garfield oynuyor ve oyuncular için şimdiden Oscar adaylığı konuşuluyor.

items.body:
Ishak Pasha Palace, an 18th-century palace in eastern Türkiye, has welcomed 200,000 visitors so far this year. Officials hope to reach 250,000 by the end of December, Hürriyet Daily News reported on Tuesday, 6 October.

The palace stands near the town of Doğubayazıt in Ağrı province, at the foot of Mount Ağrı, Türkiye's highest mountain, close to Iran. The local governor Çolak Abdi Pasha started the building, and his grandson Ishak Pasha finished it. It mixes several styles, for example Seljuk, Ottoman and Baroque. It also had central heating, which was very unusual at that time. Since 2000 it has been on UNESCO's Tentative List, a list of places that a country wants to propose as World Heritage.

More than 30,000 people came in August and 25,000 in September. Many are foreigners, from countries such as Australia, the United States, Iran and Azerbaijan. An audio guide should be ready by the end of the year, and restoration work continues.
items.title: Ishak Pasha Palace in eastern Türkiye hopes for 250,000 visitors
items.tr: Ağrı'nın Doğubayazıt ilçesindeki 18. yüzyıldan kalma İshak Paşa Sarayı bu yıl şimdiye kadar 200 bin ziyaretçi ağırladı; hedef yıl sonuna kadar 250 bin. Saraya yıl sonuna kadar sesli rehber sistemi de gelecek.

items.body:
A Dutch court has ruled that a staffing agency was wrong to fire a warehouse worker because of two pairs of underwear. The agency, Tempo-Team, must pay him €12,710, NL Times reported on Wednesday, 7 October.

A staffing agency employs people and sends them to work at other companies. The man had worked since the summer of 2024 in a warehouse that stores Calvin Klein and Tommy Hilfiger clothes. In March 2026, security guards found two Calvin Klein boxer shorts in his bag. According to the agency, the warehouse forbids workers to bring clothes of these brands to work. It fired him at once for theft.

The man said he had bought the shorts months earlier at a sale for employees. They were in his bag because he wanted to go to the gym after work. The judge decided that the agency could not prove that he wanted to steal. The money covers lost wages, compensation and legal costs.
items.title: Dutch worker fired over two boxer shorts wins €12,710
items.tr: Hollanda'da bir mahkeme, çantasında iki Calvin Klein boxer bulunduğu için hırsızlık suçlamasıyla işten çıkarılan depo işçisini haklı buldu. İş bulma ajansı Tempo-Team ona 12.710 euro ödeyecek.
